config._smoke_note: NOT A RESULT AND NEVER QUOTABLE AS ONE. Uses only the first 8000 train rows for the Gram (a different object than the sealed 138000-row spectrum) and the gates are bypassed. Its only job is to prove the code paths execute: memmap load, streaming Gram + class sums, analytic standardisation, eigh, kappa/gamma fixed points, predicted E_g(P) curves for both families, crossing detection, spectrum diagnostics, evidence write. Every number it produces is meaningless.

gate.predicted_crossing: within [1/3, 3] of the measured M116 crossing midpoint (bypassed in smoke)

kill_switch_1_crossing.registered: predicted crossing within factor [1/3, 3] of the measured M116 crossing midpoint (41400)

kill_switch_2_gap_direction.registered: predicted sparse error < dense error at n_max (matches measured accuracy order)

lambda_grid_sensitivity.note: robustness of the predicted crossing to the ridge constant (the mapping to the program's penalty is exact at lambda=1.0)

measure.standardise: per-dim mean/unit-variance over the rows used

question: does the Canatar-Bordelon-Pehlevan learning-curve theory, from the feature Gram spectra alone, predict M116's measured Q(n) crossing?

dense._tail_note: tail_index = slope of log(eta) vs log(rank) over the top half (more negative = faster-decaying spectrum = stronger spectral bias = steeper learning curve at fixed n)

sparse._tail_note: tail_index = slope of log(eta) vs log(rank) over the top half (more negative = faster-decaying spectrum = stronger spectral bias = steeper learning curve at fixed n)
